sample_unit: multiple-choice questions (each presented three times to six chatbots); plus 20 public education questions for four models

links.outcome: Reading level of chatbot responses on postpartum depression versus recommended sixth grade level
links.effect: All models produced outputs exceeding the recommended sixth grade reading level; ChatGPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro were relatively more accessible.
links.quote: All models produced outputs exceeding the recommended sixth grade reading level, although ChatGPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro were relatively more accessible.

links.outcome: Readability of chatbot outputs for patients relative to plain-language standard
links.effect: All four models exceeded the recommended sixth grade reading level; suboptimal readability may limit accessibility for users with lower health or digital literacy.
links.quote: All models produced outputs exceeding the recommended sixth grade reading level, although ChatGPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro were relatively more accessible.

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial LLM chatbots on standardized MCQs and public health questions regarding postpartum depression for accuracy, reliability, and readability, but does not test a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
